system_description.narrative_title: Fragmentation, Economic Weaponisation and an AI-Driven Reordering
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is in flux as kinetic stalemates (notably the US–Iran war) have migrated into economic and energy contestation, while rapid AI-driven investment and deployment are reshaping growth, labour and security. States are weaponising trade, sanctions and financial tools even as central banks and treasuries grapple with sticky inflation, bond-market stress and liquidity interventions; cyber operations and supply‑chain frictions amplify instability. Great‑power competition (and pragmatic cooperation) over energy, tech access and market influence cuts across regional wars and economic blocs, producing a more fragmented, multi-domain system.
system_description.scope: The interacting set of states, multinational firms, financial markets, energy flows and chokepoints, tech and AI ecosystems, international institutions, military forces, and cyber/infra actors that together determine geopolitics, global trade and systemic stability.
system_description.super_system: Global human socio-economic-technical system (planetary civilization / the Anthropocene)
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy markets & maritime security (Strait of Hormuz, oil and gas flows)
Global finance & macroeconomic policy (bond markets, central banks, treasury actions)
AI, tech industry & cybersecurity ecosystem (data centres, investment, state-linked hacking)
Regional security theatres (Middle East, Eastern Europe, East Asia) where military and proxy conflicts play out

variables.name: Iran‑centred maritime & energy conflict
variables.description: The U.S. and Iran are locked in a prolonged confrontation that has migrated into maritime attacks, tanker targeting and economic pressure around the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting oil flows and prompting regional deals to manage shipping.

variables.name: Russia‑Ukraine high‑intensity war
variables.description: Russia’s invasion and Ukraine’s resistance continue as an attritional conventional and aerial campaign reinforced by Western materiel and sanctions, shaping European security and prolonged battlefield stalemate.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic tech rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting dominance in semiconductors, AI, advanced robotics and cyberspace through trade controls, industrial policy, corporate ties and intelligence operations, reordering global tech ecosystems.

variables.name: U.S. economic coercion & trade realignment
variables.description: U.S. use of tariffs, targeted trade measures and financial pressure against allies, partners and adversaries is provoking retaliatory measures and driving a reconfiguration of economic alliances and supply chains.

variables.name: AI‑driven global economic shift
variables.description: The rapid spread of generative AI, massive data‑centre investment and platform power is altering productivity, labour markets, capital flows and cyber risk, creating new winners and systemic governance challenges worldwide.
